title: Injective resolutions exist, and a left exact functor is recovered in degree zero
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category with enough injectives and $\mathcal B$ an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. (1) Every object $X$ of $\mathcal A$ has an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions] $s:X\to I^\bullet$ with $I^q=0$ for $q<0$: a complex $I^0\xrightarrow{d^0}I^1\xrightarrow{d^1}\cdots$ of injective objects and a morphism $s:X\to I^0$ with $d^0s=0$ such that $0\to X\xrightarrow{s}I^0\xrightarrow{d^0}I^1\to\cdots$ is exact (equivalently, $s$ is a quasi-isomorphism from the complex $X[0]$ concentrated in degree $0$ to $I^\bullet$). (2) Let $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a left exact additive functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive] and $s:X\to I^\bullet$ any injective resolution with $I^q=0$ for $q<0$. Then $v(d^0)\circ v(s)=0$, so $v(s)$ factors through the degree-$0$ cycles $Z^0(v(I^\bullet))=\ker v(d^0)$, which equal $\mathcal H^0(v(I^\bullet))$ because $v(I^{-1})=0$; and the induced morphism $v(X)\to\mathcal H^0(v(I^\bullet))$ is an isomorphism.
